## Assigned Media Reflections

These are the assigned media for your 5 reflection assignments. Due dates are on Canvas.

---

### Reflection 1: The Scale of the Universe

**Module 1 — Observing the Sky**

**Watch:** *"The Most Astounding Fact"* — Neil deGrasse Tyson (3 min)
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9D05ej8u-gU>

**Or:** *"Cosmic Eye"* — a zoom from face to universe (3 min)
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Are9dDbW24>

**Connection:** Cosmic scales, our place in the universe, the "spoiler alerts" from Lecture 1

---

### Reflection 2: Seasons and Misconceptions

**Module 1 — Earth, Moon, Sky**

**Watch:** *"A Private Universe"* — Harvard graduation interviews (20 min, excerpt)
<https://www.learner.org/series/a-private-universe/>

**Why this one:** Famous documentary showing that even Harvard graduates get seasons wrong. Watch how smart people confidently give incorrect explanations — then reflect on why this misconception is so persistent.

**Connection:** Seasons, common misconceptions, the tilt explanation from Lecture 3

---

### Reflection 3: Light and Telescopes

**Module 2 — Light & Spectra**

**Watch:** *"Cosmic Queries: The James Webb Space Telescope"* — StarTalk podcast episode (45 min)
<https://www.startalkradio.net/show/cosmic-queries-the-james-webb-space-telescope/>

**Or:** Any recent JWST results video from NASA or PBS Space Time (your choice, link it)

**Connection:** Infrared astronomy, why JWST sees farther/older than Hubble, how telescopes work

---

### Reflection 4: Stellar Evolution

**Module 2 — Stars**

**Watch:** *"The Life and Death of Stars"* — PBS Space Time (15 min)
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PM9CQDlQI0A>

**Or:** *"Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey"* — Episode 8: "Sisters of the Sun" (43 min, Netflix/streaming)

**Connection:** Stellar lifecycles, HR diagram, why massive stars die young

---

### Reflection 5: Black Holes or Exoplanets (Your Choice)

**Module 3 — Galaxies & Cosmology**

**Option A — Black Holes:**
*"The Edge of All We Know"* (Netflix documentary, 99 min)
— or any Veritasium/PBS video on the 2019 black hole image

**Option B — Exoplanets:**
*"The Search for Another Earth"* — NOVA (53 min)
— or any recent video on TRAPPIST-1 or habitable zone planets

**Connection:** Extreme objects, detection methods, what we can/can't observe

---

## Propose Your Own

Found an astronomy video, documentary, or podcast you want to use instead? You can propose a substitution:

1. **Message me on Canvas** with:
   - Link to the media
   - Which reflection it would replace
   - Why you want to use it (1–2 sentences)

2. **Approval criteria:**
   - Must be astronomy-related (not general science or sci-fi)
   - Must connect to course content from that module
   - Reasonable length (5–60 minutes; documentaries up to 2 hours OK)

3. **Not allowed:**
   - TikToks under 3 minutes
   - Videos that are pure entertainment with no educational content
   - Anything you've already watched for another class

---

## Tips for Media Reflections

- **Watch actively** — take a few notes as you go
- **Don't summarize** — I know what's in the video; tell me what *you* think
- **Be specific** — name concepts, quote moments, describe scenes
- **Connect to class** — use vocabulary from lectures and readings
- **Ask real questions** — the kind you'd actually want answered

See the *Media Reflection Guide* and *Examples* handouts for more detail.
